Stage Two — Direction

Why this sequence, and not the other way around

Most personal development starts with mindset and hopes the body follows. I build it the other way around, because discipline you've proven in your body is faster to build and a lot harder to talk yourself out of.

01 — Evidence

The body proves it first

A completed set doesn't lie to you. There's no negotiating with it, and that's exactly what makes physical training the fastest way to prove to yourself that you can actually change.

For example: the push-up you couldn't finish cleanly in Week 1, done properly in Week 4. Nobody has to tell you that's real. You already know.
02 — Transfer

The pattern carries over

The same discipline you build under a bar shows up later at work, in your follow-through, in how you handle pressure. It's not an accident. It's the same trained response, just showing up somewhere new.

For example: the same person who didn't skip a 6am session starts finding it easier to have the hard conversation they'd been putting off at work.
03 — Depth

It goes quieter from there

Once your body and mind are trained together, what's left is a steadier, quieter sense of who you are underneath both. That's the third stage, and I don't wrap it in ceremony or a label.

For example: you stop needing someone to notice the work for it to count. Doing it was always going to be enough.
“What's wild in you was never meant to be tamed. Only trained.”

This framework comes from twelve years I spent living inside a disciplined, ashram-based way of life. It was a routine built entirely around training the body and mind together, and I've paired that with years of hands-on work in fitness with people in my own community. None of this is theory. It's what I watched work, again and again, and I've turned it into a structure you can actually follow too.

Week by Week

What you actually do, every week

Not a syllabus you read once and forget. Every week gives you something to test, something to keep, and someone to answer to.

Weeks 1–4

Body — Discipline

Week 01

Baseline

Measure where you actually are, honestly, before anything changes.

Week 02

Environment Design

Rebuild your surroundings so the next rep is the easy option, not the hard one.

Week 03

The Dip

Train through the week motivation runs out, and see what's on the other side.

Week 04

One number you can't argue with. Your first real mark.

Weeks 5–8

Week 08

Weeks 9–12

Being — Depth

Week 09

Movement With Intention

Week 10

Something carried the whole week, not just attempted once.

Week 11

Integration

Week 12

Close

Rewrite your recovery plan with eleven weeks of real evidence behind it. Leave with it.

Every week, the same three things: something you test, something you keep, and someone who checks — a cohort member, a partner, or a live session. Nothing here runs on your memory of reading it once.

What's Asked of You

We built the structure. This part's yours.

The programme carries the framework. It doesn't carry you. Three things are on you, every week, for twelve weeks.

  • Show up, including the weeks you don't want to — especially those
  • Do the work honestly. The artifacts are evidence for you, not performance for anyone else
  • Show up for your cohort the way you'd want them to show up for you
Before You Apply

Questions people actually ask

What is the weekly time commitment?

One 30-minute live group session each week, plus your own training days — decided individually in Week 1, based on what actually works for your schedule and body, not a fixed number handed to you.

Are the weekly live sessions recorded?

Yes. If you miss a session, a recording is shared with the cohort. We'd just ask that you keep any personal reflections shared by others in the group private.

Do I need any prior fitness experience?

No. The program is built around your own baseline, tested and set by you in Week 1 — not a fixed standard everyone is expected to start at.

Is this program for men, women, or both?

Everyone. The Ascent is built for adults generally, especially young adults, and isn't restricted by gender.

What happens if I miss a week?

There's a specific re-entry practice for exactly this, introduced partway through the program and usable any time you fall behind, during the 12 weeks or after. Missing a week doesn't mean starting over.

Do you offer one-on-one coaching instead of the group format?

Not in this phase. The cohort format is intentional — people sustain discipline better with others around them than working alone. Individual coaching may be considered in future phases.

What happens after the 12 weeks end?

Before the program closes, you build your own sustainable practice for afterward, so it doesn't depend on the cohort continuing. A next step is offered at the end, with no pressure attached.

How much does it cost, and is there a payment plan?

Pricing and payment details are shared during the application process, since terms may vary by cohort.

Do I need to share medical or health information?

Only what's genuinely useful for your trainer to know — any injury or physical limitation. This isn't collected as clinical intake, and The Ascent is not a substitute for medical or professional mental health advice.
